newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - May 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - May 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-BORSA
- Officials and top dealers are optimistic about the future of the stock exchange and say the correction will end soon.
- Ministerial committee approves the sale of heavy industrial projects for the first time.
- Morgan Stanley to invest in two local firms in the first such investment by a large merchant bank in Egypt.

- Fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial raised pre-tax profits for the first nine-months of the 1996/7 financial year to 38.46 million pounds ($11.33 million) compared to 28.73 million in the same year ago period.
- General Silos and Storage pre-tax unaudited profits for the first 10 months of financial 1996/7 rose to 62.22 million from 47.739 million for the same 1995/6 period which ended in April 1996.

- Kima/Egyptian Chemical Industries holds annual general meeting last week, forecast net profits for 1997/8 to be 25 million pounds. Profits for current year 96/7 rose to 22.54 million from 19.78 million in the previous year.
- National Development Bank share offer 29.6 percent oversubscribed.
- PACHIN/Paints and Chemical Industries forecasts 116 million pound profit in financial 1997/8. Forecasts for current year are 105 million.
- Watany Bank of Egypt to give 2.7 pound dividend. Capital raised to 105 million pounds.
- Misr Exterior Bank makes 67.98 million pound profit in calendar 1996, up from 55.67 million in the previous year.
- Egypt Arab African Bank/EAAB decided in its annual general meeting not to distribute profits and will issue bonds for 150 million pounds at a date to be announced in the second half of the year.

- Egyptian Iron and Steel discussed its strategy and plans for 1997/8 in its annual general meeting and forecast profits of about 31.47 million pounds, down from 72.54 million expected in the current year.
- Credit Foncier bond issue to open on Tuesday.

- Pfizer-Egypt to give out 1.46 pound dividend for the financial year which ended on 30 November, 1996. The firm gave 0.8 pounds per share in the previous year. The company's board is also discussing issuing free shares.
- Central Egypt Flour Mills net profits for 1996/7 expected at 33.47 million pounds, lower than 41.8 million profits for 1995/6. Net sales are also down to 506.3 million from 567.7 million.
- State to offer 20 percent of General Upper Egypt Contracting tomorrow (Monday).
- State offers 30 percent, or 300,000 shares of Nubariya Agricultural and Engineering Mechanisation at a minimum price of 24.5 pounds a share.
